source.citation: Sedra & Smith (2014). Microelectronic Circuits, 7th ed., §2.2 — inverting op-amp. Ideal G = -R_feedback/R_in; real LT1001 has finite open-loop gain (~10^6) and GBW (~0.8 MHz).

sim_completed.description: 1 if LTspice transient ran without errors, else 0

vout_pk.description: Peak |V(out)| over the steady-state window (2-5 ms)
vout_pk.T_good_source: Ideal closed-loop gain G=-10 → peak V(out) = 100mV·10 = 1.0 V. Oracle on wine LTspice 26 + LT1001 model measures 0.9999 V (essentially ideal at 1 kHz, well within LT1001's 0.8 MHz GBW). T_good 5% accommodates op-amp model variation.

gain.T_good_source: Ideal gain = R_fb/R_in = 10. Oracle measures 9.999 (LT1001 finite GBW gives barely-detectable droop at 1 kHz). T_good 5% (= 0.5 / 10) accommodates op-amp model variation.
